claims.text: The initial Ti-Ni high-entropy alloy is a single-phase solid solution in which titanium and nickel are the primary constituents.
Two-stage aging will produce a uniform distribution of coherent nanoscale precipitates in the Ti-Ni high-entropy alloy.
An intermediate-temperature aging hold will initiate nucleation of nanoscale precipitates.
A subsequent short high-temperature treatment will adjust precipitate size and distribution while optimizing coherency with the matrix.
The precipitates are likely to be Ti-rich or Ni-rich phases.
The coherent nanoscale precipitates will hinder dislocation motion.
The coherent nanoscale precipitates will stabilize the alloy microstructure at high temperatures.
Hindering dislocation motion and stabilizing the microstructure will enhance elevated-temperature yield strength.
Hindering dislocation motion and stabilizing the microstructure will improve creep resistance.
Two-stage aging tailors precipitate size, volume fraction, and coherency.
The two-stage-aged alloy will have higher yield strength than the untreated as-cast alloy.
The two-stage-aged alloy will have a lower creep rate than the untreated as-cast alloy.
The proposed benefit is expected between approximately 600°C and 800°C.
The proposed benefit is expected under cyclic-loading or oxidizing conditions.
The proposed intervention applies to high-entropy alloys in which titanium and nickel are compositionally dominant.
The untreated baseline is an as-cast Ti-Ni high-entropy alloy that retains a single-phase solid-solution microstructure.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant yield-strength improvement of approximately 10–15%, together with reduced creep rates, is designated as a falsifying outcome.
Failure to observe the expected nanoscale precipitates is designated as a falsifying outcome.
